description.narrative:
Stockholm Environment Institute, Asia Center, (SEI Asien) har ansökt om 48,14 miljoner kronor för finansiering av programmet "Strategic Collaborative Fund Phase 2 (SCF2)" som täcker Asien (med fokus på ASEAN-länderna)under perioden 2018-2022.
Programmet syftar till att stödja och påverka strategiska konferenser och workshops för att bygga regionala aktörers kapacitet, stödja lärande och utbyte inom viktiga miljö- och klimat frågor och för ökat regionalt samarbete. Fokus ligger på gränsöverskridande frågor och att främja utveckling av åtgärder och policies för att adressera problemen. Jämställdhet och mänskliga rättigheter kommer genomgående att integreras, liksom de Globala utvecklingsmålen till år 2030, SDG. Huvudintressenter är representanter från regeringar, privatsektor, civilsamhälle och akademin samt samarbete med andra regionala och internationella nätverk i Asien, Kina och Europa.
Programmet är uppdelad i fyra komponenter. Komponent 1 stöder två interregionala samarbetsplattformar (ASEF "Asia Europe Environment Forum" och CAEC "China-ASEAN Environment Center"), som är centrala för dialogen mellan Sydostasien och andra regioner (Kina-ASEAN och Asien-Europa). Komponent 2 syftar till att stärka det regionala samarbetet genom att skapa regionala plattformar och evenemang (sex regionala evenemang plus en privat sektor händelse årligen). Dessa kommer att genomföras genom ett öppet årligt ansökningsförfarande. Komponent 3 handlar om lärande och kapacitetsutveckling för regionala partnerorganisationer att integrera mänskliga rättigheters och jämställdhetsperspektiv i sina aktiviteter. Komponent 4 säkerställer en effektiv hantering av programmet.
Den totala budgeten är 48,14 miljoner kronor, fördelat över fem år.

The Stockholm Environment Institute Asia Center (SEI Asia) has applied to Embassy for funding of 48.14 million SEK to carry out the "Strategic Collaborative Fund Phase 2 (SCF2)" covering Asia and the Pacific, particularly Southeast Asia within the regional grouping of the Association of Southeast Asia Nations (ASEAN), during the period 2018-2022.
The intervention aims to support strategic events, builds capacity of regional actors and enables learning for increased collaboration in Asia-Pacific on key environmental issues, including environmental transboundary issues, and to promote policy development. The focus of intervention lies on relevant opportunities for knowledge exchange includes many stakeholders and representative from governments, private sectors, civil society and academia, and collaboration with other regional and international networks between Asia, China and Europe.
In order to reach the overall goal of intervention outcome and bridging outcome are identified. The programme outcome aims to "Enhanced regional collaboration on environment, climate change adaptation and natural resource management through sound technical and policy support and the integration of gender equality and human rights based approaches towards achieving relevant SDGs"; and bridging outcome aims to "Increased capacity of regional collaboration conveners to mainstream gender equality and a human rights based approach at programme and organizational levels".
The intervention is divided into four components, which are: Component 1 supports inter-regional cooperation platforms, which are central to the dialogue between Southeast Asia and other regions (China-ASEAN and Asia-Europe). Component 2 supports regional cooperation within Asia-Pacific based on completion basis. This component consists of coaching, financial resources as well as technical expertise to lead regional collaboration efforts towards an initiation of autonomous collaborative policy development. Component 3 is learning and capacity development to support regional partners in implementing a human rights based approach and gender mainstreaming in their collaborative activities. Component 4 ensures that SEI Asia will effectively and efficiently manage the intervention, engage with the right boundary partners, provided the appropriate level of expertise where it is needed.
Of this total budget, 48.14 MSEK, the total grants of SEK 20,400,000 (42% of total budget) will be forwards to partners under Component 1 (3,200,000 SEK in total for each forum/partner - China-ASEAN and ENVforum) and Component 2 (14,000,000 SEK in total) for different events based on completion basis. The total for direct cost is 5,550,000 SEK (12% of total budget) and the total for SEI Staff fees is 22,190,000 SEK (46% of total budget).

The intention of the Strategic Collaborative Fund Phase 2 (SCF2) programme is to enhance the regional cooperation on environment, climate change, and natural resources management in Asia. These meetings and forums aim to facilitate increased awareness of sustainable development issues which will lead to better informed decision-making at several levels for policy development, taking environment and sustainable development, gender and human rights, more into account. To achieve the goal, SCF2 will deliver under four componets, namely: Component 1: Inter-regional cooperation platforms Component 2: Regional Collaboration Component 3: Capacity Building and support Component 4: Programme Management

The following are some of the results achieved by the Strategic Collaborative Fund Phase 2 (SCF2) during 2018-2024:
- The SCF2 program supported over 70 inter-regional and regional environmental events in collaboration with 33 lead partners and 87 consortium partners. SCF2 collaborated with over 1,400 organizations, bringing together over 5,200 policymakers, women, farmers, marginalized groups, youth, business, civil society, media, and key stakeholders. Each event was designed to facilitate knowledge exchange, foster partnerships, and inspire action towards a more sustainable future.
- At the regional and global levels, SCF2's contributions were important in shaping key strategic documents and action plans, such as the ASEAN China Environmental Cooperation Strategy and Action Plan (2021-2025), as well as influencing the outcomes of major international forums. For example, the results of the supported "Regional Workshop on Pathways to Climate Resiliency, held in October 2022 at Pasay City, the Philippines, were immediately used in the consortiums engagement with the United Nations Climate Change Conference (UNFCCC) or Conference of the Parties (COP) of the UNFCCC, especially COP27 in Sharm El-Sheikh, Egypt. The other example is that SCF2 supported Yunus Thailand's on youth participation and empowerment project. The youth policy canvasses were presented at the 77th United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) High Level Side Event for Social Business and Youth, which gave them the opportunity to share their visions on a global scale. These results highlighted SCF's contributions to global and regional environmental governance and policy-making processes.
- Nationally, SCF's has contributed to policy development, for example, SCF2 supported for the Regional Dialogue Workshop on Green and Sustainable Agriculture, which was organized by Laos' Department of Policy and Legal Affairs, Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry. Through SCF2, SEI supported the government's transition to more sustainable targets and priorities. Following the consultations, the government commissioned SEI to develop a policy framework for Green and Sustainable Agriculture (GSA), a plan that reflects a shift in perspective between the Lao Ministry of Agriculture and Finance and the government.
- SCF2 catalyzed policy influence and contributed to the SDGs for climate change, gender equality, human rights, and poverty reduction. For example, SCF support to Green and Sustainable Policy in Lao PDR. Through SCF2, SEI worked to support the government in turning its sights towards more sustainable targets and priorities. The ensuing consultations led the Laos government has requested SEI to support the development a policy framework for Green and Sustainable Agriculture (GSA) a plan that reflects a shift in outlook within Laos Ministry of Agriculture and Finance and the government. The Laos government has adopted a policy framework for green and sustainable agriculture, which has been used to inform policy development at the national and provincial level.
- The SCF2 programme was designed on a gender lens and a human rights-based approach. All the supported 71 regional events incorporated gender and HRBA as reflected in the diverse participation of panels to discuss inter-sectional environmental, climate change and natural resources management issues. Specifically, at least 40% of the sessions in each event have integrated gender and HRBA into the event designs.
- SCF2 supported inter-regional forum: the China-ASEAN Environmental Cooperation (CAEC) Forum, which has received SCF2 support since the program's inception. The forum brings together high-level policymakers from China and ASEAN to discuss international cooperation on environmental challenges. The SCF2 strengthened its strategic collaboration with this forum by having SEI representatives participate in several sessions and deliver a keynote address alongside Chinese and ASEAN officials. Furthermore, through SCF2, SEI contributed to the review of the China-ASEAN Strategy and Plan of Action (2021-2025), which was adopted by ASEAN and Chinese Foreign Ministers in November 2020. SEI provided expertise support in environmental issues such as climate change, biodiversity, air, water, and solid waste pollution, which were incorporated into this Strategy, as well as provided capacity building and knowledge sharing. Following its adoption, the China-ASEAN CAEC Forum 2021 gathered policymakers to discuss and agree on actions to strengthen mutual cooperation, which lead to the development of the ASEAN-China Joint Statement on Enhancing Green and Sustainable Development Cooperation in public health, social security, economic integration, digital transformation, and sustainable development at the ASEAN China Special Submit in November 2021.
